{{Current events|year=2022|month=02|day=6|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021–2022 Russo-Ukrainian crisis]]
**[[Russia–NATO relations]]
***[[President of France|French President]] [[Emmanuel Macron]] says that a deal to "avoid war in [[Ukraine]]" is "within reach" and that it is legitimate for [[Russia]] to raise its own security concerns to [[NATO]]. Macron will meet with [[Vladimir Putin]] in [[Moscow]] tomorrow. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-60281863 (BBC News)]
*[[Afghanistan–Pakistan border skirmishes]]
**Five [[Pakistan Army|Pakistani troops]] are killed after "[[militant]]s from inside [[Afghanistan]]" opened fire on a border post in [[Kurram District]], [[Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]. The army says that it retaliated, causing heavy casualties among the militants. The [[Taliban]] [[government of Afghanistan|government]] denies that the firing came from within Afghan territory. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/five-pakistan-soldiers-killed-attack-afghanistan-military-says-2022-02-06/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021–22 South-West Indian Ocean cyclone season]]
**[[Cyclone Batsirai]], a category 4 [[cyclone]] on the [[Saffir–Simpson scale]], kills at least 10 people and [[internally displaced person|displaces]] more than 48,000 after making landfall in [[Madagascar]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/africa/20220206-cyclone-batsirai-weakens-after-hitting-madagascar-floods-expected (AFP via France24)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Honduras]]
***[[Honduran President|President]] [[Xiomara Castro]] tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/honduran-president-tests-positive-covid-2022-02-06/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea]]
***[[Prime Minister of Papua New Guinea|Prime Minister]] [[James Marape]] tests positive for COVID-19 and returns home after attending the [[2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/papua-new-guinea-pm-tests-positive-for-covid-at-beijing-olympics/6430447.html (Voice of America)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] lifts its seven-day [[quarantine]] guideline for people who had contact with positive COVID-19 patients despite reporting a record 189,071 new cases. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/russia-hits-daily-covid-record-180000-cases-82704943 (ABC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
***[[South Korea]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19 after reporting a record 38,690 new cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/south-korea-covid-19-1-million-daily-record-2482011 (CNA)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[COVID-19 protests in Canada]]
**[[Freedom Convoy 2022]]
***[[Ottawa]] Mayor [[Jim Watson (Canadian politician)|Jim Watson]] declares a [[state of emergency]] in the capital as a [[trucker]] protest against [[COVID-19 vaccine]] mandates enters its second week. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/ottawa-trucker-vaccine-mandate-insurrection-b2008839.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[2022 Costa Rican general election]]
**A [[general election]] is held in [[Costa Rica]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/2/6/costa-rica-votes-in-presidential-election-with-no-clear-favourite (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021–2022 Tunisian political crisis]]
**[[Tunisia]]n president [[Kais Saied]] dissolves the nation's Supreme Judicial Council. The Council's leaders declare the dissolution as illegal. [https://www.dw.com/en/tunisian-president-dissolves-supreme-judicial-council/a-60676059 (DW)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 Winter Olympics]]
**[[New Zealand at the 2022 Winter Olympics]]
***[[New Zealand]] [[snowboarding|snowboarder]] [[Zoi Sadowski-Synnott]] wins a gold medal in [[Snowboarding at the 2022 Winter Olympics – Women's slopestyle|women’s slopestyle]], winning New Zealand its [[New Zealand at the Olympics|first-ever gold medal]] at the [[Winter Olympics]]. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/michellebruton/2022/02/05/zoi-sadowski-synnott-earns-new-zealands-first-winter-olympics-gold-medal-with-womens-snowboard-slopestyle-win/amp/ (Forbes)] [https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/sport/460990/winter-olympics-snowboarder-zoi-sadowski-synnott-wins-new-zealand-s-first-ever-gold (RNZ)]
*[[2021 Africa Cup of Nations]]
**In [[association football]], [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] win their first international trophy after beating [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]] on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] in [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations Final|the final]] at the [[Olembe Stadium]] in [[Yaoundé]], [[Cameroon]]. Senegalese [[Forward (association football)|forward]] [[Sadio Mané]] is named the tournament's Best Player. [https://edition.cnn.com/2022/02/06/football/senegal-africa-cup-of-nations-egypt/index.html (CNN)]
